items.title: Nick Polites Interview, 1963-10-08
items.q: a chap from England, uh, a trombone player called Lou Hurd, um, told me that, uh, he wanted to try and start a band. And, um, so collected a few chaps... Lyn Dutton, the agent in England, heard some of these records and offered us this contract in 1961. So we went over to England

ctx.x: No. Yeah. Well, uh, so then when you left Frank Johnson, did you go immediately to another band or?

No, I thought that, uh, oh, well, no one's, uh, playing much, uh, worthwhile jazz now, so, uh, that's it. And, uh, um, I just didn't think that, uh, it'd be worth, uh, playing. Um, but a few months later, um, uh, a chap from England, uh, a trombone player called Lou Hurd, um, told me that, uh, he wanted to try and start a band. And, um, so collected a few chaps. They're not very good players, but, uh, were very keen. And, uh, it's the old story. Um, technique doesn't matter that much. And stuff like stuff stuff…
Did your repertoire change when you went into this Melbourne New Orleans jazz band much?
